what: Published LSTM scores on CAMELS-US that the report sets beside its own, each read at the source. A record written by the AI review (like results/sources_checked.json), not by a script: the builders read the numbers from here; nothing is typed into a document.
checked_by: an AI reviewer agent (Claude), read-only, from the publishers' pages / the preprint named under each source. No team member has read these papers yet.
how_to_word_it: Published scores are for estimating the flow of a day from the weather up to and including that day (in this report's terms: the perfect weather forecast). They are set beside our upper-bound rows only, never beside the forecast rows, and always with: other basins (several hundred across the United States against 12 in the South-East), other years, another rain product, a larger network (256 cells against 64), and - 1 day ahead - our model reads two more days of weather. 'Of the same size', never 'reproduced' or 'matched'.

kratzert2019.label: Kratzert et al., 2019a
kratzert2019.where_read: article page (sections on data, model and training) and Table 2 (image hess-23-5089-2019-t02.png)
kratzert2019.set_up: one LSTM for all basins; input sequence of 270 days = the 269 preceding days plus the day whose flow is estimated; no observed flow as input; 256 memory cells; dropout 0.4; 8 seeds
kratzert2019.loss: basin-averaged NSE loss 'NSE*': squared error divided by (standard deviation of the basin's flow + epsilon) squared, epsilon = 0.1
kratzert2019.not_verified: the initial value of the forget-gate bias in that paper (do not quote one)

kratzert2019pub.label: Kratzert et al., 2019b
kratzert2019pub.where_read: abstract on the university's publication page (Water Resources Research 55(12), 11344-11354)
kratzert2019pub.set_up: k-fold validation over basins: every basin is predicted by a model that never saw it; the flow of a day from the weather up to that day
kratzert2019pub.not_verified: the number of folds; the periods

feng2020.label: Feng et al., 2020
feng2020.where_read: preprint of the Water Resources Research paper (arXiv:1912.08949): abstract, sections 2.1-2.3 and 3.1 (pages 1, 5-6, 10, 14-15, 17-19). The journal version itself was not opened; its abstract gives the same 0.86.
feng2020.set_up: one LSTM for all basins, 256 cells, sequences of 365 days, average of 6 seeds, loss: root-mean-square error. 'Projection' model: weather and basin properties up to the day whose flow is estimated, no observed flow. DI(1): the same plus the flow observed the day before; DI(3): plus the flow observed three days before.
feng2020.not_verified: nothing in the list above; scores for single regions (for example the South-East) were not read

kratzert2018.label: Kratzert et al., 2018
kratzert2018.regions: 4 hydrological units, among them the South Atlantic-Gulf region (92 basins), the region of this project
kratzert2018.set_up: experiment 1: one LSTM per basin; experiment 2: one LSTM per region; experiment 3: the regional model fine-tuned per basin. Two LSTM layers of 20 cells, dropout 10%, 365 days of input; calibration on the first 15 hydrological years (in most cases 1 October 1980 to 30 September 1995), the rest for validation.
kratzert2018.not_verified: any score for the South Atlantic-Gulf region alone (the text gives none); the median of experiment 1

weather_up_to_the_day_estimated_no_gauge.ours: lstm_all.json sets.wf.test.summary.l3.nse_median (3 days ahead: reads the weather up to the day being forecast and no further - the like-for-like lead) and sets.wf.test.summary.l1.nse_median (1 day ahead: reads two more days)

plus_flow_observed_1_day_before.ours: lstm_all.json sets.wqf.test.summary.l1.nse_median (reads two more days of weather than the published set-up)

plus_flow_observed_3_days_before.ours: lstm_all.json sets.wqf.test.summary.l3.nse_median (like-for-like in the days read)

basin_never_seen.ours: lstm_lobo.json summary.l1 (a forecast from past weather only, 11 training basins): NOT comparable in level; quote the published number only to show what hundreds of training basins make possible
